claim_text: Нитриды молибдена обеспечивают дисперсионное твердение [в контексте процесса азотирования]

caveats.text: Mo is a weak nitride former (Group 2 in Лахтин classification) — its nitrides form only via solid-state reaction, requiring higher nitrogen supersaturation
Mo nitride precipitation is kinetically delayed and difficult due to large volume misfit with the ferrite matrix (Meka PhD thesis)
The dispersion hardening contribution of Mo₂N (γ=0.4) is significantly lower than CrN (γ=1.2), VN (γ=0.8), TiN (γ=2.0) per Лахтин Table 26
Steels without Mo can achieve excellent nitriding results using Cr, Al, V, Ti — Mo is not strictly necessary

sources.title: Лахтин Ю.М., Коган Я.Д. Теория и технология азотирования (1991)
Meka S.R. PhD Thesis: Nitriding of iron-based binary and ternary alloys (2011)
Steiner T. et al. Alloying element nitride stability in iron-based alloys (2016)
Molybdenum-Nitride Precipitation in Fe-1 at. pct Mo Alloy (2013)

reason: Mo nitrides (Mo₂N, MoN) form as nanometer-sized coherent platelets during nitriding of Fe-Mo alloys and Mo-containing steels, confirmed by Лахтин textbook, Meka PhD thesis, and journal papers. However, Mo is a weak nitride former with delayed precipitation kinetics and modest hardening contribution (γ=0.4).
fragile_points: Mo nitride precipitation is kinetically delayed — at short nitriding times or low Mo content, Mo may remain in solid solution
Mo is typically used at 0.25-1% in commercial steels — its contribution is secondary to Cr, Al, or V nitrides
questions_for_author: What specific Mo nitride phase (Mo₂N vs MoN) and what size/distribution range are you assuming?
At what minimum Mo concentration does Mo nitride dispersion hardening become experimentally measurable?
Is the claim intended to mean Mo nitrides are the primary hardening mechanism, or that they contribute alongside other nitride formers?
